# Forward Deployed Product Engineer — The Walt Disney Company

---
**Job ID:** 10158258
**Date Posted:** Sep 14, 2026
**Date Applied:** Sep 15, 2026
**Salary Range:** $117,500–$157,500 per year — Glendale, CA or Burbank, CA
---

## Job Summary

An early-career product-builder role in Disney Enterprise Technology's Applied AI Acceleration practice. The engineer works directly with business stakeholders across Marketing, Finance, Parks Operations, HR, Studios, and other areas to identify worthwhile problems, build practical AI-powered products, and ship features end to end. The small team works in office Monday through Thursday and specifically asks applicants to include a portfolio link showing something they have built.

---

## What You'll Do

- Build and ship AI-powered features from problem definition through production.
- Work directly with stakeholders to understand business needs and gather feedback.
- Own user experience across workflows, interfaces, automation, and human-in-the-loop decisions.
- Use LLM APIs, prompt design, RAG, agents, and evaluation methods to solve problems.
- Build within Disney's enterprise systems using appropriate security, monitoring, and operational practices.
- Test changes before launch with regression checks, golden sets, and other evaluation methods.
- Contribute reusable code, tools, and patterns for future engagements.
- Partner through code reviews, debugging, and shared problem solving.
- Explain technical decisions and tradeoffs clearly to business stakeholders.

### Required Qualifications
- Minimum three years shipping software products for real users, including at least one year shipping AI-powered features in production
- Technical product development
- Experience with prompt design, agents, RAG, LLM APIs, and evaluations
- Daily or frequent use of AI coding tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, or similar tools
- Ability to read and reason about code, debug with teammates, and work with data using SQL, APIs, or basic transformations
- Strong product and business judgment connecting features to user needs and business outcomes
- Strong learning agility and comfort with new tools and changing technology
- Ability to communicate clearly with senior stakeholders
- Preferred: experience as a product manager, designer, operator, engineer, founder, or builder using AI tools to create working products; building AI products without a dedicated engineering team; forward-deployed engineering; design-engineering instincts; cross-business work; production evaluation methods; strong writing; and enterprise-scale data, legacy systems, or complex stakeholder environments

### Education
A bachelor's degree and/or equivalent work experience.

### Benefits
A bonus and/or long-term incentive units may be included, along with a full range of medical, financial, and other benefits depending on level and position offered.

---

## How I Match Up

### At Application — Sep 15, 2026

- **Technical product development is the strongest match:** the record shows repeated end-to-end ownership from user or customer need through design, integration, commercialization, training, support, and improvement. ICARUS-Lite, Gen3 POSEIDON, KRAKEN, the LabVIEW QC platform, and the internal ERP/CRM are all supported examples.
- **Product judgment and user-workflow evidence is concrete:** PROTEOR Print combines remote operation, live video, AI-assisted diagnostics, and production metrics in a user-facing interface developed with an external partner. The LabVIEW system turns networked sensor data into live tolerances and traceable PDF reports, while after-sales support and customer training provide direct feedback loops.
- **Founder/operator and enterprise overlap:** CTO and RJB.Engineering ownership experience align with Disney's preference for builders and operators. Kubernetes, ERP/CRM development, Microsoft Business Central, Docker, network/VLAN work, risk analysis, global collaboration, and vendor coordination support the complex-enterprise side of the role.
- **The software/LLM requirements remain a significant gap:** the evidence does not establish three years shipping conventional software products or one year shipping LLM-based AI features in production. It also does not substantiate production RAG, LLM APIs, agents, SQL, regression/golden-set evaluation pipelines, trace analysis, LLM-as-judge, Cursor, Claude Code, or formal code reviews. The resume uses supported language such as AI-assisted diagnostics and local LLM tooling rather than converting those adjacent skills into unsupported claims.
- **Education is satisfied:** the posting accepts a bachelor's degree and/or equivalent experience, and the record includes a completed B.S. in Electro-Mechanical Engineering.

### Now — Sep 19, 2026

- No material change to the match since application. Product engineering, workflow design, automation, commercialization, enterprise infrastructure, and stakeholder-facing delivery remain strong; the role's production software tenure and modern LLM application-stack requirements remain the principal gaps.
- Since Sep 15–16, 2026 the record additionally states that Riley is "quick to pick up, apply, and integrate new technologies into real-world systems" (the rewritten summary) and acts as Hiring Manager for engineering roles — supporting, not new, evidence for the builder/operator and stakeholder side of this posting.

---

## About the Company

The role is with Disney Worldwide Services within The Walt Disney Company (Corporate). Disney describes Enterprise Technology as the group delivering technology aligned to business strategy, enterprise efficiency, cross-company innovation, consumer experience, business growth, and operational excellence.
